standard_driverless_nonzero_alt_restorat.finding: No general standard Linux6.8 USBFS userspace operation both sets a nonzero alternate and leaves all claims released with no driver. This is not a blanket impossibility assertion for malformed descriptors or genuine reset failures.

code_chain.fact: usbfs_driver is an ordinary USB driver, with no release-preserve-alt flag.
RELEASE clears the owning ps.ifclaimed bit and calls usb_driver_release_interface; SETINTERFACE runs checkintf, which auto-claims an otherwise unclaimed interface.
driver release invokes usb_unbind_interface. Nonzero alternate triggers usb_set_interface(...,0); failed reset only records needs_altsetting0. soft_unbind does not skip this later alternate reset.
Interface-recipient standard CONTROL also calls checkintf; it does not evade claim/release semantics.
usb_set_interface is the driver-owned operation that updates hardware, HCD endpoint state, cur_altsetting and sysfs. Sending a wrong-recipient raw control would not be a valid substitute.
bAlternateSetting is a read-only sysfs attribute.

limitations: A descriptor with no alt0, a real device STALL/reset failure, or deferred reset can preserve nonzero cached alternate after unbind. Therefore do not add a blanket discovery or registration rejection for every driver=None/nonzero-alt interface.

A failed temporary kernel probe could legitimately leave an unbound nonzero-alt interface; usb_probe_interface error cleanup itself has no SetInterface0. That is a useful future guest-only setup candidate, not a demonstrated recovery path.

A new kernel ABI or narrowly scoped kernel helper could in principle provide a properly locked release-and-preserve-alt operation; this requires a separate privilege, kernel compatibility, security and validation design. Ordinary userspace/rooting the whole server does not change the current release semantics.

Preflight should communicate exact-restoration capability and retain the strict ownership/grant contract; rejecting the requirement is not a functionality fix. No preflight policy or production behavior was changed in this research.

facts: Public portable Interface::release documents best-effort/disconnected-error suppression; preserve that contract.
LinuxInterface::release consumes the last Arc, drops the value and returns Ok. The Drop ioctl error is only debug-logged. physical release_all therefore cannot see a real kernel failure.
physical release_all also currently collapses any visible error to a boolean State error instead of preserving first errno.

A successful RELEASE ioctl does not prove the nested alternate-reset succeeded, because usb_unbind_interface still returns0 after recording needs_altsetting0. Independent final state verification remains necessary.
minimal_safe_change: Add Linux-only Interface::release_checked using the existing Blocking wrapper; require final Arc and return Busy without ioctl when references survive.
Use a small private one-shot attempted state. Set it before the real RELEASE call. Checked success or failure must prevent Drop from implicitly sending another release.

Map actual Errno into nusb Error::new_os and preserve os_error. A release error must prevent CONNECT. Optional auto-reattach is attempted only after successful release and its true error is also returned.
Keep legacy release/Drop best effort. No new unsafe, pointer handling, dependencies or production mock facade.

physical release_all must await every remaining interface, preserve the first actual errno, skip SET_CONFIGURATION after release failure, then perform only already-designed independent reconciliation. Temporary alternate restoration must use checked release too.
pure_regressions: Busy/shared owner performs zero ioctl operations
checked success/error each attempts release once and Drop does not retry
ENODEV/EINVAL/EIO retain os_error; failed release never CONNECTs
release-before-CONNECT order and CONNECT failure visible
multi-interface release awaits later interfaces after first error and preserves the first errno

future_guest_cause_chain: Stop the first server IF0 RELEASEINTERFACE at real syscall-entry after ordinary server received SET_CONFIGURATION2.

Only dedicated guest root writes the selected IF0 to usbfs/unbind. This runs usbfs driver_disconnect and clears the original server FD ps.ifclaimed bit. Record this explicitly as external intervention.
After resume the unmodified real RELEASEINTERFACE executes; releaseintf sees no bit and returns actual EINVAL/-22. No register, syscall argument or return-value rewriting is needed.

The second interface release must still complete. SET_CONFIGURATION2 must never execute after that first error. Reobserve actual config1; ownership/grant reconciliation can safely reacquire currently unbound interfaces and restore original drivers.
UNLINK mode retains real A=-22 and UNLINK0. EOF mode has no old-wire completion requirement and must retain request budget until the true operation terminal and cleanup.

source_basis.fact: usbfs driver_disconnect clears ps.ifclaimed and cancels interface requests.
Missing original FD ifclaimed bit returns EINVAL; proc_releaseinterface propagates it.
Driver unbind invokes the same usbfs disconnect path.

independent_raw_assertions_recommended: Keep exact entry/exit TID, FD, PID starttime, node metadata and generation; gate at syscall-entry does not prove kernel-internal active.

Record separate before-intervention and release-fault snapshots. Only IF0 may intentionally change usbfs to None; config1/generation/node/FD/IF1 usbfs and budget remain strict. Do not relax other operations held-state checks.
Because no legitimate configuration change is needed in this case, assert zero SETCONFIGURATION ioctl entries for the entire trace. This proves no SETCFG2 without decoding an argument pointer.

After first target release exits -22, require a second release exit0 before any reclaim. Together with source BTreeMap0→1 ordering and independent IF1-usbfs observation, this proves subsequent IF1 release and excludes implicit IF0 retry (which would again return -22).
Require actual trace return -22 and strict wire -22/UNLINK0 or EOF resource retention; do not accept generic failure, early EOF, or State/-5.
Preserve old-product baseline FAIL and actual old wire result, followed by fixed-product validation with exact binary/source provenance.
Only after original generation/config1/alt0,1/two cdc_ether drivers and pending/queued/inflight/budget0 independent verification may cleanup count as PASS.
